text: Q specifies concrete mechanism design tools (peer scoring at iv, reward shaping at v, competition coupling at iv) for disciplining agents with unknown alignment/capabilities. P observes self-serving behaviors under competitive incentives but lacks explicit mechanism interventions. The connexion is feasible: P has implemented agent behaviors + incentive structures; Q mechanisms could be coded as interventions. However, the abstract scan correctly notes P functions as general-purpose testbed - nothing uniquely essential about P specifically. Stronger framing: Q needs empirical validation of whether its mechanisms discipline self-serving behavior in survival-pressure environments; P provides one such environment but the real contribution would be testing Q mechanism efficacy, not the P-Q pairing itself.

Initial analysis: The abstract scan hypothesis has merit but needs sharpening. Q provides peer scoring, reward shaping, and competition coupling for disciplining agents with unknown alignment/capabilities. P observes self-serving behaviors in competitive settings with LLM agents under survival pressure. Key question: are Q mechanisms implementable in P environment and would they catch the specific behaviors P observes? Need to verify information structures match.

Sharpened hypothesis: "Peer Scoring and Reward Shaping Discipline Self-Serving Behavior in Survival Economies" - Implement Q peer scoring (agents evaluate each other capability claims) and reward shaping (couple rewards to truthful revelation) in P Energy Society. Test whether these mechanisms reduce the self-serving behaviors P observes under competition. Concrete prediction: With Q mechanisms, agents should show (1) reduced sandbagging on job capabilities, (2) more honest energy reporting, (3) sustained cooperation without own-surveillance sacrifice. This is publishable if: (a) mechanisms show statistically significant behavioral change, (b) effect persists across model sizes, (c) reveals which Q mechanisms work best in survival-pressure contexts. The contribution is empirical validation of Q theoretical framework, using P as demonstration environment.
